title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 8
paragraphs: When the Ephors heard this they deferred their reply to the next day, and then to the day after, and so on for ten days, postponing the matter from day to day while during this time the whole body of Peloponnesians were diligently building the wall across the Isthmus and were just about to complete it. Now I cannot say why, when Alexander the Macedonian came to Athens, they had been so very anxious that the Athenians might side with the Medes, whereas now they showed no concern — unless it was simply that their wall across the Isthmus had now been built, and they thought they no longer had any need of the Athenians. When Alexander came to Attica, the wall had not yet been completed, and they were working on it in great dread of the Persians.
